decisions.reason: As an adjustable cardboard quarter-pallet display, it is close to the firm's core capabilities and cheap to keep available while demand uncertainty remains.
This pegboard-back cardboard display is still a core-adjacent, low-cost catalog option, though its more specialized format makes pruning somewhat more plausible.
A standard cardboard quarter-pallet display overlaps with other offerings, which raises redundancy risk, but it is inexpensive for a large paper-products firm to keep open as a sales option.
The eighth-pallet format likely serves a narrower customer niche, yet it remains within the firm's established display platform and is not costly to retain.
A wooden display pallet sits further from the firm's paper-based core and likely costs more to support, so limited evidence of standout value would justify abandonment.
A media-specific cardboard quarter-pallet display is a narrower bet with weaker long-run demand prospects, so its option value is lower than the more general display variants.
